common_name: Cherokee Gold Tomato (Golden-Orange Beefsteak, Cherokee Series)

planting.note: Start indoors 6–8 weeks before last frost and transplant into fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; stake or cage the indeterminate vine as it grows.

directions: Transplant into fertile, well-drained soil in full sun after frost risk passes, staking the vine as it grows. Cherokee Gold belongs to the celebrated Cherokee family of heirloom beefsteaks alongside Cherokee Purple and Cherokee Chocolate, distinguished by large, smooth, golden-orange fruit with the same rich, complex, low-acid flavor and meaty texture that made the original Cherokee Purple a modern heirloom classic. The bright, sunny color makes it a favorite for mixed heirloom tomato platters and salads alongside its darker-fruited siblings, and the indeterminate vine produces reliably over a long season. Water evenly through fruit development to reduce cracking on the smooth skin, and harvest once color deepens to full gold for the sweetest, most complex flavor.

common_name: German Head Tomato (Large Meaty German Heirloom Beefsteak)

planting.note: Start indoors 6–8 weeks before last frost and transplant into deeply worked, fertile soil in full sun; the heavy fruit clusters need sturdy staking or caging from an early age.

directions: Transplant into deeply worked, fertile soil in full sun after frost risk passes, staking or caging early to support the heavy fruit. German Head is a German heirloom beefsteak grown for enormous, smooth, pink-red fruit with dense, meaty, low-seed flesh and a rich, sweet, well-balanced flavor typical of the great German pink beefsteak tradition that also produced varieties like German Johnson and German Pink. Individual fruit regularly tops a pound, making it an excellent slicing tomato for sandwiches and fresh eating, and the indeterminate vine remains productive over a long season when given consistent water and feeding. Provide sturdy support for the heavy fruit clusters, and water evenly through fruit development to reduce cracking on the large, smooth-skinned fruit.

common_name: Italian Heirloom Tomato (Large Ribbed Sweet Pink Beefsteak)

planting.note: Start indoors 6–8 weeks before last frost and transplant into fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; stake or cage the indeterminate vine as it grows.

directions: Transplant into fertile, well-drained soil in full sun after frost risk passes, staking the vine as it grows. Italian Heirloom was preserved and shared through the Seed Savers Exchange network from a family's own long-held Italian seed stock, producing large, distinctively ribbed and slightly flattened, deep pink-red fruit with sweet, well-balanced, richly flavored flesh reminiscent of classic Italian slicing tomatoes. The pronounced ribbing and irregular shoulders give the fruit an old-world, rustic appearance that sets it apart from the smoother modern hybrids most gardeners are used to, while the vigorous indeterminate vine produces reliably through a long season. Water evenly through fruit development to reduce cracking around the ribbed shoulders, and harvest once fruit fully colors for the best flavor.

common_name: Pink Berkeley Tie Dye Tomato (Marbled Pink-Green Striped Beefsteak)

planting.note: Start indoors 6–8 weeks before last frost and transplant into fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; stake or cage the indeterminate vine as it grows.

directions: Transplant into fertile, well-drained soil in full sun after frost risk passes, staking the vine as it grows. Pink Berkeley Tie Dye is a modern open-pollinated variety related to the original green Berkeley Tie Dye, bred by Wild Boar Farms and prized for its striking exterior of pink and green streaks and blushes, which give way when sliced to a marbled, jewel-toned interior of pink, red, and gold swirled together in a genuinely tie-dye pattern. Beyond the visual novelty, the flavor is rich, sweet, and complex, ranking among the better-tasting of the modern striped 'tie dye' tomato series that has become popular with heirloom and specialty tomato growers. The indeterminate vine is productive over a long season; water evenly through fruit development to reduce cracking, and harvest once the distinctive coloring fully develops.

common_name: Kosovo Tomato (Balkan Heirloom Meaty Pink Beefsteak)

planting.note: Start indoors 6–8 weeks before last frost and transplant into fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; stake or cage the indeterminate vine as it grows.

directions: Transplant into fertile, well-drained soil in full sun after frost risk passes, staking the vine as it grows. Kosovo is a Balkan heirloom valued for large, smooth, pink-red, slightly oxheart-shaped fruit with dense, meaty, low-seed flesh and a mild, sweet flavor, and it is notably productive for a tomato of its size, setting a heavier crop than many other large-fruited heirlooms of similar fruit weight. The low acidity and thick, low-moisture flesh make it especially good for slicing and sandwiches, since the fruit holds together well without excess juice. The vigorous indeterminate vine benefits from sturdy staking to support the heavy fruit load; water evenly through fruit development to reduce cracking, and harvest once fruit fully colors for the best flavor.
